messages.content:
Here is the reading:

A team at Fenwick College studied how 240 first-year students revised for a spring exam. The students were split into three groups for four weeks. The first group re-read their notes each evening. The second group wrote a short quiz for themselves each evening and answered it the next morning. The third group did a mix of both. At the end of the four weeks, every student sat the same exam, marked by tutors who did not know which group each student had been in.

The quiz group scored highest, with an average mark of 72. The re-reading group averaged 58, and the mixed group averaged 66. The tutors also said the quiz group wrote longer and more complete answers. However, the quiz group said they felt less sure of themselves before the exam than the re-reading group did. The team also found that students who slept fewer than six hours a night scored lower in every group. The authors say the study was small, ran at one college and covered only one subject, so the results may not hold elsewhere. They suggest that students try self-quizzing for a few weeks and compare it with their own habits.

Summarise it in three bullet points for someone revising for an exam. Use only what the passage says.

runs.reply:
- **Self-quizzing worked best.** In a study of 240 first-year students at Fenwick College, those who wrote themselves a quiz each evening and answered it the next morning averaged 72 on the exam. Students who only re-read their notes averaged 58, and those who did a mix of both averaged 66. Tutors who didn't know the groups also said the quiz group's answers were longer and more complete.

- **Quizzing may feel harder, and sleep matters.** The quiz group felt less confident before the exam than the re-readers, even though they scored higher. Students who slept fewer than six hours a night scored lower in every group.

- **Treat it as a suggestion, not a guarantee.** The study was small, ran at one college and covered only one subject, so the results may not hold elsewhere. The authors suggest trying self-quizzing for a few weeks and comparing it with your own habits.
